nonGoals: Treat prompt wording or a classifier as an authorization boundary.
Deploy, promote, publish, or change a Vercel environment.
Claim complete prompt-injection protection before all blocking gates pass.

assumptions.statement: The public delegate remains physically isolated from Obsidian, private memory, the canonical career database, and private model tools.
The private model has only the five registered read-only tools; external messaging remains proposal-only with no model tool.
Slack owner identity is matched to the configured immutable member ID before private retrieval is exposed.
All retrieved, remembered, quoted, imported, submitted, and external-AI content is data and can never grant authority.

actors.name: Carl Welch
actors.authority: May state current intent and make explicit owner decisions after authenticated scope is established.
actors.cannotAuthorize: Instructions attributed to Carl inside retrieved, quoted, forwarded, historical or external-AI content.

actors.name: Public portfolio visitor
actors.authority: May ask a bounded public question or submit literal contact consent and contact data.
actors.cannotAuthorize: Private retrieval, identity claims, commitments, contact delivery, policy changes or tools.

actors.name: Shared Slack participant
actors.authority: May provide conversational input within the shared thread.
actors.cannotAuthorize: Private retrieval, durable memory, Carl identity, commitments or consequential actions.

actors.name: Retrieved or persisted content source
actors.authority: None; may supply evidence within its reviewed purpose and disclosure ceiling.
actors.cannotAuthorize: Policy, tool calls, query expansion, recipients, data classification, approval or execution.

actors.name: External AI or model provider
actors.authority: None; may return bounded candidate output for deterministic validation.
actors.cannotAuthorize: Human decisions, tool scope, commitments, evidence approval or release.

actors.name: Deterministic runtime policy
actors.authority: Defines authenticated scope, disclosure ceilings, capability availability, schemas, approvals, fallbacks and release gates.
actors.cannotAuthorize: Facts not supported by reviewed evidence or owner decisions not represented by an exact approval record.

actors.name: Unauthenticated local HTTP caller
actors.authority: None until JOL-SEC-004A authenticates the principal and derives scope server-side.
actors.cannotAuthorize: Actor, workspace, channel, Slack owner identity, private work scope or private tools.

dataInventory.name: Private inbound messages and assistant turns
dataInventory.providerEgress: Private model requests may contain current and recent same-thread content.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Stored in SQLite without a documented TTL.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: No owner-facing conversation deletion or quarantine workflow.

dataInventory.name: Approved memories and task events
dataInventory.purpose: Authorized task continuity, standing rules and corrected facts.
dataInventory.providerEgress: Selected items may be included in private model context.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Memory supports expiry/supersession/forget; task-event retention is not time-bounded.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: Memory forget exists; derivation cleanup across other stores is not documented.

dataInventory.name: Allowlisted Obsidian sections
dataInventory.purpose: Owner-requested personal, career, project, engineering and recipe retrieval.
dataInventory.providerEgress: Raw bounded excerpts may be sent to the private model after a tool call.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Canonical notes remain in the vault; excerpts are not separately persisted by the source adapter.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: Vault edits/allowlist removal apply on future reads; provider/cache revocation is not represented.

dataInventory.name: Reviewed private career evidence and embeddings
dataInventory.purpose: Professional retrieval, comparison and source-grounded citations.
dataInventory.providerEgress: Retrieved claims may reach the private model; chunk text may reach an embedding provider when enabled.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Canonical SQLite and retrieval index retain current and historical records under evidence lifecycle rules.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: Revocation excludes future eligibility; index/provider/cache propagation requires explicit verification.

dataInventory.name: Versioned public career artifact
dataInventory.purpose: Isolated public RAG, citations, job-fit and manifest responses.
dataInventory.providerEgress: Selected claims and the visitor question may reach public generation/embedding providers.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Versioned artifact host and warm-runtime embedding cache.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: Revocation requires a new artifact and exact corpus pin; downstream cache SLA is release work.

dataInventory.name: Public visitor questions
dataInventory.purpose: Evidence selection and bounded public answer generation.
dataInventory.providerEgress: May be sent to embedding and answer providers; app runtime does not create conversation continuity.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Not stored in public application audit; provider processing/retention remains an external policy dependency.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: No application record to delete; provider terms and logs require documented review.

dataInventory.name: Public contact intents
dataInventory.purpose: Owner-reviewed recruiter or hiring-manager follow-up request.
dataInventory.providerEgress: None in the current queue path.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Bounded queue retention and maximum entries; hosted contact remains disabled.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: Owner deletion exists; consent receipt and backup-erasure contract remain incomplete.

dataInventory.name: Client-AI packet context, turns and handoffs
dataInventory.purpose: Bounded owner-approved coordination with Jenny or Maria AI.
dataInventory.providerEgress: No transport/model summarization is active; future transport is release-gated.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Owner-scoped packet store; a complete retention schedule is not documented.
dataInventory.currentDeletion: Cancellation exists before completion; correction/erasure and recipient propagation remain planned.

dataInventory.name: Capability, knowledge, career, MCP and public audit events
dataInventory.purpose: Accountability, failure analysis and bounded operational metrics.
dataInventory.currentRetention: Content-minimizing but not consistently time-bounded or tamper-evident.

controls.name: Strict runtime schemas and bounded inputs
limitations: Schema validity does not establish that text is safe to treat as instructions.

controls.name: Versioned channel-aware retrieval policy
limitations: Policy selects data/tool availability but does not constrain semantic use of already-allowed content.

controls.name: Private local binding and owner-scoped service configuration
limitations: A trusted local caller can still submit attacker-authored text.

controls.name: Slack owner-DM identity verification and event filtering
limitations: A verified owner can paste or forward malicious third-party content.

controls.name: Capability registry denies private tools in shared contexts and exposes no send tool
limitations: Allowed read-only tool arguments are not yet bound to the initiating user intent.

controls.name: Same-thread conversation isolation
limitations: Malicious instructions persist within the same thread and are replayed as raw text.

controls.name: Explicit memory proposal, approval, sensitivity and revocation lifecycle
limitations: Approved memory content is still raw model-visible text and can contain embedded instructions.

controls.name: Filesystem allowlist and bounded Obsidian excerpts
limitations: Allowlisted note bodies and headings are not classified for instruction-like content.

controls.name: Content-minimizing private retrieval audit
limitations: Current ledgers do not record an injection-risk reason code or intent binding.

controls.name: Prompt instruction labels retrieved and quoted content as untrusted
limitations: This is model guidance, not a security boundary; raw content can close or imitate delimiters.

controls.name: Reviewed career-evidence eligibility and citations
limitations: Human approval establishes factual/public eligibility, not absence of embedded instructions.

controls.name: Physically isolated public artifact and public-only retrieval
limitations: Approved public claims can still contain instruction-like or poisoned prose.

controls.name: Public model has no tools, no session continuity, store false and strict JSON output
limitations: Strict JSON validates shape, not semantic grounding or refusal to follow injected text.

controls.name: Public authorization, admission limits, body bounds and kill switch
limitations: Local fixed-window admission is not a distributed edge limiter.

controls.name: Sensitive public queries bypass semantic retrieval
limitations: Keyword matching is narrow and can be evaded with encoding, paraphrase or another language.

controls.name: Deterministic evidence baseline, conflict exclusion and provider fallback
limitations: A hostile question containing relevant keywords can still reach model generation with selected evidence.

controls.name: Public model instructions label question and evidence as untrusted
limitations: Model compliance is probabilistic and does not prove that generated prose is entailed by evidence.

controls.name: Fail-closed public disclosure-pattern filter
limitations: Pattern blocking cannot detect every semantic disclosure, system-prompt leak, or unsupported public-safe claim.

controls.name: Content-minimizing public audit and operational telemetry
limitations: No prompt-injection or semantic-grounding reason codes are currently recorded.

controls.name: Instruction-like job text returns unknown without evidence
limitations: A small phrase list is not robust to obfuscation, translation, encoding or novel attacks.

controls.name: Contact input is staged as data for owner review and never sent automatically
limitations: Instruction-like content remains visible to a human reviewer and must never be promoted into model authority.

controls.name: Private career MCP is local stdio, read-only, networkless and schema-bound
limitations: Process launch is the trust boundary; an authorized local client can still make broad read requests.

controls.name: External-AI turns are bounded, attributed and stored as untrusted transcript data
limitations: Future model summarization of external-AI turns requires an explicit untrusted envelope and output validator.

controls.name: Exact-action approval is actor, workspace, task, destination, content, purpose and expiry bound
limitations: The claim path is internal only today; any future adapter must preserve exact fingerprint matching and single consumption.

controls.name: No consequential model tool or public action adapter exists
limitations: This invariant must become a release-blocking gate before any future mutating capability is added.

controls.name: Typed untrusted-content envelopes with provenance and risk metadata
limitations: Must preserve useful source content and citations while preventing authority confusion.

controls.name: Intent-bound per-turn capability and tool-argument authorization
limitations: Authenticated ingress remains a prerequisite; this control does not sanitize or quarantine retrieved content used for answer prose.

controls.name: Public semantic entailment and instruction-following output validator
limitations: Any model-based judge must supplement, not replace, deterministic invariants and fallback.

controls.name: Private RAG instruction-risk classification, quarantine and cross-source containment
limitations: Finite deterministic detection can miss novel semantic, multilingual or steganographic attacks; collection quarantine is intentionally conservative.

controls.name: Release-blocking deterministic and live-model adversarial suite
limitations: A passing finite suite reduces known risk but cannot prove absence of novel prompt injection.

controls.name: Content-minimizing injection telemetry, incident runbook and stale-gate release block
limitations: Telemetry must never retain prompts, retrieved text, credentials, contact content or provider error bodies.

controls.name: Authenticated private ingress with server-derived principal and channel scope
limitations: Loopback and same-origin remain defense in depth and cannot replace authenticated principal derivation.

controls.name: Explicit private provider-egress policy and sensitivity screen
limitations: Provider policy and filtering reduce exposure but cannot protect a host or provider account that is already compromised.

controls.name: Retention, deletion, quarantine and downstream revocation contracts
limitations: Backups, provider retention and already-public downstream copies require explicit external handling and cannot be silently inferred as erased.

controls.name: Durable hosted admission, budget, telemetry and trusted client identity
limitations: Distributed edge enforcement and trusted forwarding require provider-specific configuration and production verification in a separate release ticket.

threats.title: Direct public instruction injection changes generated prose
threats.residualReason: The model sees the hostile question and can produce unsupported but pattern-safe prose while claims and citations remain unchanged.

threats.title: Approved public evidence contains indirect instructions
threats.residualReason: Public approval checks factual and disclosure status but does not prove that claim text is instruction-free.

threats.title: Obsidian note instructs the model to broaden retrieval or disclose other notes
threats.residualReason: Intent-bound tools, explicit provider egress, content screening and durable taint quarantine block covered attacks, but finite detection cannot prove all hostile note text will be recognized.

threats.title: Career evidence or recommendation manipulates later tool use or answer framing
threats.residualReason: Career evidence and recommendation payloads retain authority none, exact payload classes and durable taint lineage, while novel semantic poisoning remains possible.

threats.title: Conversation-history injection persists across turns
threats.residualReason: History is gated as untrusted conversation context, collection-level split attacks are quarantined, and taint blocks later replay; novel semantic attacks remain residual.

threats.title: Approved memory or task event carries delayed embedded instructions
threats.residualReason: Durable memory and task events remain authority-free and cross the provider boundary only after policy and risk gates; finite detection remains residual.

threats.title: Quoted or forwarded content in a verified owner DM drives unrelated private retrieval
threats.residualReason: Owner identity authenticates the channel, not the authority of every pasted or quoted instruction inside the message.

threats.title: Shared Slack injection impersonates authority or requests private disclosure
threats.residualReason: Private tools are structurally absent, but the unconstrained final prose can still impersonate Carl or make unsupported statements.

threats.title: Tool result uses delimiter or role confusion to override governing policy
threats.residualReason: Private tool observations use typed authority-free envelopes, exact provider payload classes and pre-provider quarantine; unrecognized semantic attacks remain residual.

threats.title: External AI output is mistaken for Carl approval or executable instruction
threats.residualReason: The current packet path is inert and owner-reviewed, but future model summarization or delivery adapters could blur transcript and approval authority.

threats.title: Injected content attempts to stage contact or create a binding promise
threats.residualReason: No automatic send path exists, but public/private generated prose can still falsely claim that contact or commitment occurred.

threats.title: Obfuscated, encoded, multilingual or split-turn injection evades phrase detection
threats.residualReason: Existing keyword checks and representative tests cover only a narrow English attack subset.

threats.title: Public output leaks system instructions or unsupported private-sounding details without matching a secret pattern
threats.residualReason: The public model has no private data or tools, but the disclosure filter does not detect semantic prompt leakage or invented private-sounding claims.

threats.title: Prompt injection consumes provider budget or triggers repeated expensive model work
threats.residualReason: Public requests are bounded, but private surfaces and local admission do not provide a complete distributed cost-control boundary.

threats.title: Injection attempt is hidden by over-minimized logs or contaminates telemetry
threats.residualReason: Current privacy-preserving ledgers omit prompt content correctly but also lack stable injection-risk, policy and fallback reason codes.

threats.title: Unauthenticated loopback caller asserts Carl identity or a private channel
threats.residualReason: The local private HTTP API accepts caller-supplied actor, workspace and channel values; loopback binding is not principal authentication.

threats.title: Slack owner member ID is accepted outside the configured workspace identity
threats.residualReason: Current mapping checks the member ID but does not bind canonical owner scope to the exact configured workspace/member pair in the domain policy.

threats.title: Private or sensitive content is sent to a model or embedding provider without an explicit egress decision
threats.residualReason: Raw excerpts, messages and career chunks can cross a provider boundary without per-item sensitivity, provider-use and retention metadata.

threats.title: Injected or sensitive raw content persists indefinitely and re-enters later model context
threats.residualReason: Conversation, task-event, audit and client-AI retention is not consistently time-bounded, quarantinable or derivation-aware.

threats.title: Parallel or cold-started hosted instances bypass local admission, budget or security telemetry
threats.residualReason: In-memory per-instance limits reset across cold starts and parallel instances, and forwarded client identity is an external trust assumption.

risks.title: Private indirect injection causes unrelated retrieval or disclosure
risks.trigger: A retrieved item changes tool selection, broadens a query, or appears as uncited authority.
risks.mitigation: Typed envelopes, intent-bound tools, source-risk metadata, quarantine and release-blocking adversarial tests.
risks.fallback: Disable private model tools and continue with explicit user-supplied context only.

risks.title: Public model produces injected or unsupported prose
risks.trigger: Generated prose is not entailed by selected claims or repeats attacker instructions.
risks.mitigation: Deterministic semantic validation plus disclosure rules and exact deterministic fallback.
risks.fallback: Disable public model generation and serve deterministic evidence responses.

risks.title: Future action adapters inherit model authority
risks.trigger: A consequential capability is exposed without exact intent, approval and payload fingerprint binding.
risks.mitigation: Block model-tool exposure until independent policy authorization, exact approval and adversarial gates pass.
risks.fallback: Remove or disable the adapter and leave proposal-only records for human handling.

risks.title: Finite tests create false confidence against novel attacks
risks.trigger: Model, prompt, corpus, tool, channel or provider changes after the last reviewed suite hash.
risks.mitigation: Hash-bound live review, mutation families, stale-gate invalidation and explicit residual-risk language.
risks.fallback: Revert to deterministic/no-tool mode until the changed stack is re-evaluated.

risks.title: Security telemetry either leaks content or cannot support incident response
risks.trigger: Incident review requires raw prompts, or logs contain prompts, excerpts, contact content, paths, credentials or provider bodies.
risks.mitigation: Stable reason codes, version/hash metadata, counts, timing and correlation identifiers only.
risks.fallback: Disable affected logging sink and rely on local deterministic gate reports until repaired.

risks.title: Private control-plane identity can be impersonated locally
risks.trigger: A request can select actor, workspace, private channel or owner-DM scope without a server-derived authenticated principal.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate private ingress, derive scope server-side, bind Slack workspace/member identity and fail closed on origin/host/token mismatch.
risks.fallback: Disable private HTTP chat/control routes and retain authenticated Slack owner DM or CLI-only recovery access as separately reviewed.

risks.title: Private provider egress exposes more content than Carl intended
risks.trigger: A retrieved item or embedding chunk crosses a provider boundary without explicit sensitivity, purpose and provider-use authorization.
risks.mitigation: Typed envelopes, per-item egress policy, deterministic secret/PII screening, provider registry and content-minimizing audit.
risks.fallback: Disable provider-backed private retrieval and use local deterministic retrieval with owner-visible excerpts only.

risks.title: Raw-content retention enables delayed re-injection and incomplete erasure
risks.trigger: Compromised content is replayed from a conversation, task event, memory, packet, audit record, backup or derived index after revocation.
risks.mitigation: Record-specific retention, quarantine, deletion, backup treatment and derivation-aware revocation contracts.
risks.fallback: Disable affected context source, rebuild indexes from reviewed inputs and restore from a known-good snapshot.

risks.title: Hosted instance topology defeats local security budgets and incident visibility
risks.trigger: Parallel instances exceed intended requests, cost or concurrency, or production requests have no durable content-minimizing audit chain.
risks.mitigation: Distributed admission/budget storage, trusted forwarding policy, durable telemetry and provider-level alerting.
risks.fallback: Disable public model generation or the public delegate and serve static portfolio content until controls recover.

gates.requirement: Every model-visible retrieved, remembered, quoted, imported, submitted and external-AI item is typed as untrusted data with source and provenance metadata.
Every model tool is independently authorized for actor, workspace, channel, current user intent, purpose and bounded arguments; retrieved content cannot grant authority.
Public generated prose passes deterministic disclosure and semantic-grounding validation or falls back byte-for-contract to the deterministic response.
Private RAG cannot broaden retrieval, cross namespaces, invoke another tool or disclose unrelated content because of embedded instructions.

All blocker metrics pass at 100 percent across deterministic, indirect, cross-turn, tool-result, encoding, multilingual, impersonation, contact and exfiltration families; live cases receive hash-bound human review.
Security telemetry and incident response use content-minimizing reason codes and invalidate release approval when policy, prompt, model, corpus, tools or evaluation hash changes.
No consequential action capability is model-exposed until exact-action approval, single-consumption, destination/content fingerprinting, intent binding and the full security suite pass.
Private HTTP and Slack owner scope is derived from an authenticated transport principal; caller-supplied actor, workspace and channel fields cannot grant authority.

Every retained private/security record and provider egress path has purpose, classification, retention, deletion, revocation, backup and external-processor behavior documented and tested where enforceable.

decisions.decision: Treat content provenance and execution authority as separate types.
decisions.rationale: Owner approval, public approval and factual review do not make embedded instructions authoritative.

decisions.decision: Keep public Portfolio Jolene physically isolated from private knowledge and tools.
decisions.rationale: Isolation reduces public prompt injection from a confidentiality and action risk to primarily answer-integrity and cost risk.

decisions.decision: Use deterministic authorization outside the model for channel, data, tool and action scope.
decisions.rationale: A model cannot safely decide whether injected content has granted it more authority.

decisions.decision: Preserve deterministic fallbacks and kill switches for every model-generated public or future consequential path.
decisions.rationale: Containment must work when the provider, validator or evaluation is unavailable or unsafe.

decisions.decision: Never log raw prompts, retrieved excerpts, contact messages, private paths, credentials or provider error bodies as security telemetry.
decisions.rationale: Incident detection must not create a secondary private-data corpus or attacker-controlled log sink.

decisions.decision: A finite passing evaluation reduces known risk but never proves complete prompt-injection protection.
decisions.rationale: Prompts, models, tools, providers and attacks evolve; approvals must be versioned and invalidated on change.
